texts.li: [first] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the Waystone Book open at the colony's page. Written there in red: the colony {TALE}, and {ENEMY} were the ones wronged. {COUNT} silver pays them back, {X_pronoun} says, by the league's hand; or the colony may send someone to argue the entry, or refuse it, and every league will deal with it as the book says.

[first,lowtech] A factor of {FACTION} in a dusty coat, {X_nameDef}, has stopped at the gate and opened the Waystone Book on {X_possessive} knee. Fair dealers in good ink, robbers in red, {X_pronoun} reads, and the colony's page is red: it {TALE}, and {ENEMY} were the ones wronged. {COUNT} silver would pay them back.

[first,!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has driven up to the gate with the league's ledger on the seat beside {X_objective}. The colony's page is in red ink: it {TALE}, against {ENEMY}. {COUNT} silver, carried to them by the league, would settle it; {A_nameDef} could argue the entry instead, if the colony thinks it wrong.

[first,war] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the Waystone Book. The colony {TALE}, and though {ENEMY} are its enemies now, the league writes what is done to traders on the road in red all the same. {COUNT} silver pays them back.

[again] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is back at the gate with the Waystone Book, open at the same red page: the colony {TALE}, against {ENEMY}, and it has not paid. {COUNT} silver settles it still, and every league deals with the colony at worse terms until it does.

[twice] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come back with the Waystone Book, where the colony's wrong is written twice now: it {TALE}, against {ENEMY}. {COUNT} silver settles it, {X_pronoun} says, and nothing less.

li.label: Pay {ENEMY} back ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, who writes the colony's page clean in good ink and will carry it to {ENEMY}.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to argue the entry
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} argued the entry over the book at the gate, and {X_nameDef} struck it out.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} argued the entry, and {X_nameDef} wrote it twice for the arguing: the colony owes double now.

li.label: Refuse the entry
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} closes the book on the red page and rides on, and the league will deal with the colony at worse terms until it pays.

lines.li: [paid] Good ink, then, and the road is open.
[struck] Struck out, and may I never have to write it again.
[twice] Twice in red, and the next page is worse.
[red] The book remembers, even when I forget.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a waymaster of {FACTION}, has walked up to the gate with a surveyor's chain over {X_possessive} shoulder. With {TALE} going through the region, the league would lay its stretch across the colony's land: a gang camped at the edge for some days, a stretch of {BEAST} a day. The line runs past the gate; {X_pronoun} asks the colony's leave.

[fields] A waymaster of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the gate with the line for {TALE} drawn on a map. It crosses the colony's ground and runs over its fields, {COUNT} cells of them, unless they go round; {X_pronoun} asks whether the gang may lay it through.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a staff notched for every day's stretch. The league's road for {TALE} is packed earth, rammed down by hand, and its line runs across the colony's land; {X_pronoun} asks the colony's leave to lay it there.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a waymaster of {FACTION}, has come up the road with the gang's stone carts behind {X_objective}. They are laying {TALE} in flagstones of the land's own stone, and the line runs across the colony's land; {X_pronoun} asks the colony's leave.

[age2] A truck of {FACTION}'s road gang has pulled up short of the gate, and {X_nameDef}, the waymaster, has walked over with the plans. {TALE} goes down in concrete, a stretch a day, and its line crosses the colony's land; {X_pronoun} asks the colony's leave.

[age3] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with the line for {TALE} glowing on a slate: paved tile, a stretch a day, across the colony's land and past its gate. The league asks the colony's leave before it lays a single tile.

[their:grateful] The league writes the colony in good ink, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask its leave first: {TALE} would run across its land, laid by a gang camped at the edge, a stretch of {BEAST} a day.

li.label: Lay it across our land, fields and all
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the gang; the road will cross the colony's land the straightest way, over its fields where the line runs.

li.label: Lay it across our land, round the fields
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the gang; the road will cross the colony's land and go round its fields.

li.label: Not across our land
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} rolls up the line without a word for it, and the gang will lay the road round the colony's land.

lines.li: [leave] A stretch a day, and you'll watch it grow.
[leave] Edda Vane would have liked a road like this.
[round] Round it is, and the long way.

IncidentDef.label: nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy

texts.li: [litters] Hospitallers of {FACTION} have come up to the gate with litters on their shoulders, {X_nameDef} at their head. The fight is over, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and {COUNT} of the raiders still lie where they fell; the order would carry them to its sickhouse, for nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy.

[cart] A stretcher cart of {FACTION}'s order has stopped at the gate, and {X_nameDef} has climbed down with the bearers. {COUNT} of the raiders lie downed on the colony's land; the order would carry them away to its sickhouse, if the colony lets them go.

[one] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a litter and a bearer. One of the raiders still lies out there, and {X_pronoun} asks to carry {ENEMY}'s fallen to the order's sickhouse, for nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy.

[many] Hospitallers of {FACTION} are at the gate with litters, {X_nameDef} at their head. {COUNT} lie downed out there, of {ENEMY} and others; the order would carry every one of them to its sickhouse, and ask nothing for it.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a hospitaller of {FACTION}, has come over the field with two bearers and a pair of poles and blankets. Aldith's lamp hangs over the sickhouse door for anyone, {X_pronoun} says, and {COUNT} of the raiders lie out there still.

li.label: Let them carry them all away
li.outcome: The hospitallers are going out with their litters, and will carry every one of the fallen raiders off the colony's land.

li.label: Only the worst hurt
li.outcome: The hospitallers carry off the worst hurt of the raiders; the rest are the colony's to deal with.

li.label: They are the colony's to keep
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says nothing, writes it down in the order's book, and leads the bearers away.

lines.li: [carry] Lift together, gently, and mind the head.
[carry] Nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy.
[kept] It is written, and that is all.
[gone] The lamp is lit for them now.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a satchel of the order's. {TALE} is spreading in the colony, {A_nameDef} has it and {COUNT} in all, and {X_pronoun} asks for a sick room: the sick kept together in {PLACE}, the well staying out, and {X_objective} dosing them on rounds for three days.

[herbs] A sister of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come in with a bundle of herbs and boiled linen. Word of the colony's {TALE} reached the order, {X_pronoun} says; give {X_objective} {PLACE} for a sick room three days, and the sickness will have a harder road.

[masks] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate in a mask, with a case of the order's. {TALE} is going round the colony, {COUNT} down with it; {X_pronoun} would keep a sick room in {PLACE} for three days, with the colony's own medicine.

[nodoctor] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has heard the colony has {TALE} and nobody well enough to nurse it. {X_pronoun} asks for {PLACE} as a sick room, three days of rounds, and the well kept out.

[lowtech] A sister of {FACTION} has walked in over the fields, {X_nameDef}, with Aldith's lamp hung from {X_possessive} staff. Where {TALE} goes, {X_pronoun} says, a sick room follows: {PLACE} for three days, and {X_objective} to dose the sick on rounds.
[their:grateful] The order remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come as soon as word of its {TALE} came: three days of rounds in a sick room, {PLACE}, if the colony will have it.

li.label: Give {X_objective} {PLACE} as a sick room
li.outcome: The sick are going to {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} is setting out the order's things for the first round.

li.label: Give {X_objective} {PLACE}, {B_nameDef} on the rounds too
li.outcome: The sick are going to {PLACE}, and {B_nameDef} will walk the rounds with {X_nameDef} and learn the order's ways.

li.label: Thank {X_objective}; the colony will manage
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} leaves a little of the order's herbs at the gate and walks back the way {X_pronoun} came.

lines.li: [room] The well stay out, and the sick stay in, and we'll see.
[round] Drink this, all of it, and then sleep.
[caught] It has caught me too, and now I am the one in bed.
[goes] It has a harder road now, and I have a long one.
[thanks] Keep them warm and keep them apart.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. With {TALE} on the region, the order would pitch a field sickhouse by the colony: a long hut of beds, a lamp at its door all night, and the region's sick and wounded brought to it. They would ask for medicine, food and clean cloth, and maybe for the colony's doctor.

[plague] A sister of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has walked up to the gate in a mask. {TALE} has the region by the throat, {X_pronoun} says, and the order needs ground for a sickhouse where the sick can reach it; the colony's is good ground.

[war] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate after {TALE}, with the order's lamp unlit on a pole. The wounded of the region have nowhere to lie, {X_pronoun} says, and the order would raise a long hut of beds by the colony and light the lamp at its door.

[oursick] {X_nameDef}, a sister of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a cart of bedding. With {TALE} on the region, the order would pitch a sickhouse by the colony, and the colony's own sick could lie in it too.

[lowtech] Sisters of {FACTION} have come up the road with poles and bedrolls, {X_nameDef} carrying Aldith's lamp. After {TALE}, they would raise a long hut by the colony for the region's sick, and hang the lamp at its door for anyone.
[their:grateful] The order remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask its ground first: a field sickhouse by the colony while {TALE} lasts, the lamp lit at its door all night.

li.label: Let them pitch it by the colony
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the sisters, and the order will raise its sickhouse by the colony.

li.label: Let them, and take our sick in too
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the sisters; the order will raise its sickhouse by the colony, and the colony's own sick will lie in it.

li.label: Not by our gate
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods, and goes to find the order other ground.

lines.li: [pitch] The lamp goes up tonight, and stays lit.
[thanks] Somewhere else, then, and soon.
[home] Home now, and gently.
[bell] One ring for the one who goes home.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION}, has walked up to the gate ahead of the herd. A drove of {COUNT} head of {TALE} would cross the colony's land, {X_pronoun} says, and graze it two or three days on the way, their fire at the far edge; they ask the colony's leave.

[fields] A drover of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the gate with a long stick and a dog at heel. {COUNT} head of {TALE} would cross the colony's land and graze as they go, and the colony's unfenced fields lie near their way; {X_pronoun} asks its leave all the same.

[ride] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has ridden up to the gate, the drove raising dust behind. {COUNT} head of {TALE}, two or three days across the colony's land and grazing it, their fire at the far edge; {X_pronoun} asks the colony's leave.

[lowtech] A drover of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has walked to the gate barefoot, the drove lowing at the edge. A guest eats from the same pot, {X_pronoun} says, and asks to bring {COUNT} head of {TALE} across the colony's grass two or three days.
[their:grateful] The herding folk remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask it first: {COUNT} head of {TALE} across its land, two or three days, grazing as they go.

li.label: Let them cross
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back for the drove; it will cross the colony's land and graze its way to the far edge.

li.label: Let them cross, for a toll ({BEAST} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts out the toll at the gate without a word and goes back for the drove.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} turns back to the drove, and the drovers will take it round the colony's land.

lines.li: [cross] Count them with us at dusk, if you like.
[round] Round it is, and the grass is thinner there.
[ride] Ride at the edge with me, and keep them moving.
[on] Up and on, every head of you.

IncidentDef.label: the thief on the drove road

titles.li: The thief on the drove road

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a warden of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate at first light with riders behind. {ENEMY} drove off {TALE} of the colony's yesterday, and the herders found the trail at dawn. They would follow it to the thieves' camp; the colony could send {A_nameDef} with them, or let them go alone, and they would bring back what they can.

[ride] Herders of {FACTION} have ridden up to the gate in the morning, {X_nameDef} at their head. The thieves who took {TALE} from the colony left a trail a child could follow, {X_pronoun} says; {A_nameDef} could ride with them to the camp, or they could ride alone.

[many] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with riders: {ENEMY} drove off {COUNT} head of the colony's, {TALE}, and the herders count every beast at dusk, theirs or a friend's. They are on the trail now, and would have {A_nameDef} with them.

[!ride] Herders of {FACTION} have walked in on the thieves' trail at first light, {X_nameDef} with a spear and a coil of rope. {ENEMY} drove off {TALE} of the colony's, and they mean to follow; {A_nameDef} could walk with them, or they go alone.

[lowtech] A warden of {FACTION}'s herders, {X_nameDef}, is at the gate with riders and a dog that has the scent. {TALE} of the colony's went off with {ENEMY}, and the herders would have them back; {A_nameDef} could come along, or they go by themselves.

li.label: {A_nameDef} rides with them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is going out with the herders' riders on the thieves' trail.

li.label: Let them ride alone
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the riders are off on the trail, and will bring back what they can.

li.label: Let the beasts go
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shakes {X_possessive} head over the lost beasts, and the riders go home.

lines.li: [together] Keep up, and keep low when we come close.
[alone] We count every head at dusk, and yours too.
[thanks] Lost beasts are lost, and the grass grows anyway.
[back] Here they are, and one stays with us for the trail.
[charge] Now, all together, and take the beasts first.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate. It is calving time, {X_pronoun} says, and the colony's ground is sheltered: they would bring {COUNT} beasts in calf to camp on it some days, until the calves are on their feet.

[age0] An old herder of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has walked to the gate with a hand on a heavy cow's flank. {COUNT} of the herd are near their time, and the colony's ground is out of the wind; {X_pronoun} asks to camp on it until they have calved.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with the spring. Every head is counted aloud at dusk in their camps, {X_pronoun} says, and soon there will be more to count: {COUNT} beasts in calf, some days on the colony's sheltered ground.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate with a ledger of the herd. {COUNT} beasts are due to calve this month, and {X_pronoun} asks to bring them to the colony's sheltered ground for it.
[their:grateful] The herding folk remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has brought their beasts in calf to it first this spring: {COUNT} of them, some days on its sheltered ground.

li.label: Let them calve here
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is going back for the herd, and the herders will camp on the colony's sheltered ground for the calving.

li.label: Let them, for a toll ({BEAST} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts out the toll at the gate without a word and goes back for the herd.

li.label: Not this spring
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back to the herd to find other ground before the calves come.

lines.li: [calve] More to count at dusk, soon enough.
[thanks] They'll calve where they stand, then, and we'll manage.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has come up from the calving camp at a run. One of their {TALE} is calving and it is going hard, {X_pronoun} says, and asks for the colony's best hand at beasts, {A_nameDef}, before it is too late.
[second] {X_nameDef} of the calving camp is at the gate, sleeves rolled. A {TALE} is stuck in a hard birth, and {X_pronoun} asks for {A_nameDef}; {B_nameDef} could come and learn from it too.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}'s herders has come to the gate with bloody hands. A {TALE} has been labouring since dawn, and the herders have done all they know; {X_pronoun} asks whether {A_nameDef} would come.
[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} has come up from the calving camp with a lamp and a coil of rope. A {TALE}'s calf is turned wrong, {X_pronoun} says, and asks for {A_nameDef}'s hands at it.
[their:grateful] {X_nameDef} of the calving camp has come to the gate: a {TALE} is in a hard birth, and the herders trust the colony's {A_nameDef} with it more than themselves.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} is going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}, though the birth is turned badly.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes, {B_nameDef} beside {A_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are going down to the calving camp with {X_nameDef}, though the birth is turned badly.

li.label: The herders know their beasts
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back down to the camp to see it through with the herders.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} goes back down to the camp to see it through with the herders, though it is turned badly.

lines.li: [come] Quick now, and warm your hands first.
[manage] We've done this since before the drove roads.

texts.li: Two pilgrims of {FACTION} have come to the gate, {X_nameDef} with a staff hung with shells. They have found something holy on the colony's ground, the {TALE}, and would set stones and a lamp beside it and bless it: three days' work, and an old shrine for the colony that pilgrims will stop at.

[ancient] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has stopped at the gate with another pilgrim. The {TALE} out on the colony's land is older than any of the peoples, {X_pronoun} says, and holy for it; they would set stones and a lamp beside it, and bless it.

[grave] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have come to the gate from the {TALE} on the colony's land, older than the colony. Nobody blessed it, {X_nameDef} says, and asks leave to set stones and a lamp beside it, and bless it.

[tree] {X_nameDef} and another pilgrim of {FACTION} have come in from the great old {TALE} on the colony's ground. A tree that old has heard a great many prayers, {X_pronoun} says; they would set stones and a lamp under it and bless it.

[landmark] Two pilgrims of {FACTION} have come to the gate from the far side of the colony's land. {TALE} is holy to the fellowship, {X_nameDef} says, and they would set stones and a lamp where it can be seen, and bless it.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, nearly blind and led by a younger pilgrim, has stopped at the gate. Old Brannoc blessed every door, {X_pronoun} says, and a holy place on the colony's land has no stones yet; three days, and it would have stones and a lamp.
[second] Two pilgrims of {FACTION} have found the {TALE} on the colony's land and would set stones and a lamp beside it, three days' work, or two if {B_nameDef} worked beside them.

li.label: Let them raise it
li.outcome: The pilgrims are walking out to the {TALE} with their stones, and will set them three days.

li.label: Let them, {B_nameDef} working beside them
li.outcome: The pilgrims are walking out to the {TALE} with their stones, {B_nameDef} beside them, two days' work.

li.label: Leave the place as it is
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} blesses the gate on the way out, open or shut, and the pilgrims walk on.

lines.li: [raise] A stone for every prayer said here before us.
[thanks] Bless this door, open or shut.
[day] Another course of stones, and the lamp tomorrow.
[bless] Blessed, and lit, and the colony's now.
[stop] A little for the road, and a little left here.

texts.li: [clash] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a shell on a cord. Word reached the fellowship that {TALE} and {DEAD} quarrel in the colony; {X_pronoun} would have everyone at one table this evening, {A_nameDef} to speak for the one and {B_nameDef} for the other, and bless it.

[split] A palmer of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has stopped at the gate. {TALE} is near a split in the colony, {X_pronoun} has heard, its believers wavering; this evening at one table {A_nameDef} could speak for those who are sure and {B_nameDef} for those who are not, and the palmer would bless it.

[clash,lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a palmer in a frayed cloak, has come in to the gate at dusk. Old Brannoc blessed every door, open or shut, {X_pronoun} says, and {TALE} and {DEAD} could share a table for one evening, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speaking.

[split,lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a palmer of {FACTION}, has walked to the gate with a staff hung with shells. A faith that wavers needs a table more than a sermon, {X_pronoun} says; {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} could speak for {TALE} this evening, and the palmer would bless the meal.

[their:grateful] The fellowship remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come as soon as word came of its faiths: one table this evening, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speaking, and a blessing over it.

li.label: Gather this evening; {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} speak
li.outcome: The colony will gather at one table this evening, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to speak and {X_nameDef} to bless it.
li.riskOutcome: The colony gathered at one table, and {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spoke, but it did not hold.

lines.li: Bread for both sides of the table.
Let each speak, and the other listen.
One table, and one evening of it.
Bread for both sides of the table.
Let each speak, and the other listen.
One table, and one evening of it.

li.label: Let {X_objective} bless each side apart
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will walk about the colony and bless the believers of each side one by one, no speeches.

li.label: Thank {X_objective}, and send {X_objective} on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} blesses the gate on the way out, open or shut, and walks on.

lines.li: [table] One table, and room at it for everyone.
[walk] Each in turn, then, and no speeches.
[thanks] Bless this door, open or shut.
[settled] It held, and may it hold a season.
[split] It did not hold, and that is said plainly.
[bless] Steady now, whatever you believe.
[apart] Every one of them blessed, and the road is long.
